report:
# Correcting the Premise: Hydroxychloroquine Does Not Reduce COVID-19 Mortality

Based on the strongest available scientific evidence, the answer is actually **no** — hydroxychloroquine does not reduce the likelihood of dying from COVID-19. The randomized controlled trial data, which is far more reliable than early observational studies, consistently show no mortality benefit.

**Key evidence:**

1. **RECOVERY Trial** (UK, one of the largest COVID-19 platform trials, published in *NEJM*): Randomized 1,561 patients to hydroxychloroquine and 3,155 to usual care. There was **no significant difference in 28-day mortality** between groups; the hydroxychloroquine arm was stopped early due to lack of benefit (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2022926).

2. **WHO Solidarity Trial**, involving over 30 countries and thousands of hospitalized patients, found hydroxychloroquine "produced little or no reduction in mortality" compared to standard care, leading WHO to halt this treatment arm (https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/coronavirus-disease-covid-19-hydroxychloroquine).

3. **NEJM analysis of WHO interim results** confirmed that both Solidarity and RECOVERY — the two largest trials — "showed no benefit" on mortality from hydroxychloroquine in hospitalized patients (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7727327/).

4. **Cochrane systematic review**, regarded as a gold-standard evidence synthesis, concluded that hydroxychloroquine "has little or no effect on the risk of death" in COVID-19 patients and probably has no effect on progression to mechanical ventilation (https://www.cochrane.org/fr/CD013587/INFECTN_la-chloroquine-ou-lhydroxychloroquine-est-elle-utile-pour-traiter-les-personnes-atteintes-de-la).

**Bottom line:** Early enthusiasm based on small, non-randomized studies suggested possible benefit, but large randomized trials and rigorous meta-analyses (the gold standard for causal evidence) consistently found no reduction in COVID-19 mortality from hydroxychloroquine. Major health authorities (WHO, NIH, FDA) recommend against its use for COVID-19 treatment.
